questions.prompt: When a scientist looks carefully at something happening in nature and notes what they see, this first step is called making an:
questions.explanation: An observation is the careful noting of what is seen in nature, and it usually leads to the question that starts an investigation.

questions.prompt: A student records the mass of seedlings on a balance and draws a line graph of mass against time. The graph and the recorded masses are best described as the experiment's:
questions.explanation: The recorded measurements and the graph drawn from them are the data, the evidence later used to draw a conclusion.

questions.prompt: A team tests a medicine by giving real pills to one group and identical-looking sugar pills to another, with neither group told which they received. The main purpose of the sugar pills is to:
options: Make the study cheaper to run
Increase the number of people who recover
Act as a control so any effect of the real medicine can be separated from belief alone
Replace the need to repeat the test
questions.explanation: The dummy (placebo) pills are a control group; comparing them with the treated group shows whether the medicine itself, not just the expectation of treatment, caused any change.

questions.prompt: About what fraction of the mass of a living human body is made up of water?
questions.explanation: Water makes up roughly two thirds of the mass of the human body, which is why it is so important for life.

questions.prompt: Two simple sugar units are joined together by a condensation reaction. The molecule formed is best described as a:
questions.explanation: Two sugar units joined together form a disaccharide; many joined together would form a polysaccharide.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares the building blocks of lipids and proteins?
options: Lipids are built from fatty acids and glycerol, while proteins are built from amino acids
Both are built only from glucose units
Lipids are built from amino acids, while proteins are built from nucleotides
Both are built from mineral ions
questions.explanation: Lipids are made from fatty acids and glycerol, whereas proteins are polymers of amino acids; the two groups have different building blocks.

questions.prompt: What is the name for the new substance that is formed after an enzyme has acted on its substrate?
questions.explanation: The product is the new substance made when an enzyme converts its substrate during a reaction.

questions.prompt: Why is it correct to say an enzyme is denatured rather than killed when it is destroyed by heat?
options: Because enzymes are not alive, so they cannot be killed; heat instead destroys their shape
Because enzymes turn into living cells when heated
Because killed and denatured mean exactly the same thing
Because heat makes enzymes reproduce too quickly
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not living organisms, so they cannot be killed; heat permanently destroys the enzyme's shape, which is called denaturation.

questions.prompt: An enzyme reaction speeds up steadily as more substrate is added, but eventually the rate stops rising even though more substrate is still being added. The best explanation is that:
options: All the enzyme active sites are already busy, so adding more substrate cannot speed things up further
The enzyme has turned into substrate
Substrate slows enzymes down at high amounts
questions.explanation: Once every active site is occupied, the enzymes are working as fast as they can, so extra substrate must wait and the rate levels off.

questions.prompt: A food company wants an enzyme to keep working inside a hot industrial tank at 80 degrees Celsius, where ordinary human enzymes would fail. The most suitable source of such an enzyme would be an organism that:
options: Lives at normal human body temperature
Naturally lives in very hot springs
questions.explanation: Enzymes are adapted to the temperature of their organism's environment, so a microbe from hot springs is likely to have enzymes whose shape survives high temperatures.

questions.prompt: What is the jelly-like material inside a cell where many chemical reactions take place?
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance filling the cell, and it is where many of the cell's chemical reactions occur.

questions.prompt: Which feature is shared by a bacterial cell and a plant cell but is absent from a typical animal cell?
questions.explanation: Both bacterial and plant cells have a cell wall, while animal cells do not; bacteria lack a true nucleus, which plant cells have, so that is not shared.

questions.prompt: A large permanent vacuole in a plant cell is mainly responsible for:
options: Storing cell sap and helping keep the cell firm
questions.explanation: The large vacuole stores cell sap and, when full, presses outward to help keep the plant cell firm and the plant upright.

questions.prompt: A scientist measures a cell and finds it is only about two micrometres across and contains no membrane-bound organelles. The cell is most likely:
options: A fungal cell with a nucleus
questions.explanation: Very small size and the absence of membrane-bound organelles are typical of prokaryotic cells such as bacteria, which are much smaller and simpler than eukaryotic cells.

questions.prompt: A root hair cell takes in water and dissolved minerals from the soil but does not photosynthesise. Which statement about its likely structure is most reasonable?
options: It is packed with chloroplasts to make food
It has a cell wall and cell membrane but few or no chloroplasts, since it gets no light underground
It has no cell membrane so water can flood in freely
It is a prokaryotic cell with no nucleus
questions.explanation: As a plant cell it still has a cell wall, membrane, and nucleus, but because it grows underground in the dark it gains nothing from chloroplasts, so it has few or none.

questions.prompt: Which green pigment inside chloroplasts traps the light energy used in photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light energy to drive photosynthesis.

questions.prompt: Which raw material for photosynthesis is taken up by a plant mainly from the soil rather than from the air?
questions.explanation: Water is absorbed from the soil through the roots, while carbon dioxide comes from the air; light is energy, not a material taken from the soil.

questions.prompt: After a long-distance run, a person keeps breathing heavily for several minutes even though they have stopped moving. This extra oxygen is mainly needed to:
options: Break down the lactic acid that built up during the run
Make more lactic acid in the muscles
questions.explanation: During hard exercise muscles respire anaerobically and build up lactic acid; afterwards extra oxygen is taken in to break this lactic acid down, so breathing stays heavy for a while.

questions.prompt: A potted plant is sealed in a clear box and kept in bright light. Over several hours the amount of carbon dioxide in the box falls. The best explanation is that:
options: The plant has stopped respiring completely
Carbon dioxide has turned into nitrogen
Respiration in the plant is producing oxygen
Photosynthesis is using up carbon dioxide faster than respiration releases it
questions.explanation: In bright light photosynthesis runs faster than respiration, so the plant takes in more carbon dioxide than it releases, and the level in the box falls.

questions.prompt: Which row correctly states where each process happens and whether it releases or stores energy?
options: Photosynthesis in mitochondria, releases energy; respiration in chloroplasts, stores energy
Both happen only in the nucleus and both store energy
Photosynthesis in chloroplasts, stores energy in glucose; respiration in mitochondria, releases energy from glucose
Respiration in chloroplasts releases energy; photosynthesis in mitochondria releases energy
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts and stores the Sun's energy in glucose, while respiration occurs in mitochondria and releases that stored energy for the cell to use.

questions.prompt: A normal human body cell has 46 chromosomes arranged in pairs. How many pairs of chromosomes is this, and where in the cell are they found?
options: 12 pairs, found in the cell membrane
questions.explanation: Forty-six chromosomes form 23 pairs, and they are held inside the nucleus, which controls the cell.

questions.prompt: An organism that has two identical alleles for a gene, such as TT or tt, is described as:
questions.explanation: Homozygous means the two alleles for a gene are the same (TT or tt); heterozygous would mean they are different, such as Tt.

questions.prompt: A homozygous tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a short pea plant (tt), where tall is dominant. What are the offspring expected to be?
questions.explanation: Every offspring receives a T from one parent and a t from the other, so all are Tt; because tall is dominant, they all appear tall.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to know whether a black bull (black is dominant) is homozygous BB or heterozygous Bb. The most useful cross to find out is to mate it with cows that are:
questions.explanation: Crossing the bull with white (bb) cows reveals its genotype: if any calves are white, the bull must carry a recessive b allele and is heterozygous; if all calves are black, he is likely homozygous.

questions.prompt: In a plant, red flower colour (R) is dominant over white (r). A grower crosses a heterozygous red plant (Rr) with a white plant (rr). What ratio of red to white flowers is expected in the offspring?
questions.explanation: An Rr by rr cross gives half Rr (red) and half rr (white), a 1 red : 1 white ratio.

questions.prompt: A horse and a donkey can mate, but their offspring (a mule) is almost always unable to have young of its own. Using the biological meaning of a species, this tells us that horses and donkeys are:
options: Two different species, because their offspring are not fertile
questions.explanation: A species is a group that can breed together to produce fertile offspring; because the mule is infertile, the horse and donkey count as two separate species.

questions.prompt: A feature that has been inherited and helps an organism survive in its environment, such as a thick coat in a cold place, is called an:
questions.explanation: An adaptation is an inherited feature that improves an organism's chance of surviving and reproducing in its particular environment.

questions.prompt: When the last individual of a species dies and the species no longer exists anywhere, this is called:
questions.explanation: Extinction is the permanent loss of a species, which happens when none of its members survive to reproduce.

questions.prompt: Many different mammals, such as a human arm, a whale flipper, and a bat wing, share the same basic arrangement of bones even though they are used for different jobs. Biologists use this as evidence that these animals:
options: Were all created at exactly the same moment
Share a common ancestor from which they evolved
Cannot be related in any way
questions.explanation: A shared underlying bone pattern despite different uses suggests the animals inherited it from a common ancestor and then evolved in different directions.

questions.prompt: On an island, a long drought kills most plants except those with deep roots that reach water. After several generations, deep-rooted plants dominate the island. Which sequence best describes how natural selection produced this result?
options: Variation in root depth already existed; deep-rooted plants survived the drought and passed on the helpful alleles, so they became common
The drought forced each plant to deliberately grow deeper roots within its own lifetime
The plants moved to find water and changed species
All plants on the island were identical, so chance alone decided
questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on existing variation: plants that already had deeper roots survived and reproduced, passing the advantageous alleles on, so the trait spread through the population.

questions.prompt: The stomach contains muscle tissue, lining tissue, and nerve tissue all working together to digest food. Using the levels of organisation, the stomach itself is best described as an:
questions.explanation: Several different tissues working together form an organ, so the stomach is an organ; many organs together (like those of digestion) form an organ system.

questions.prompt: Which part of a balanced diet is needed in large amounts mainly to help food move through the gut and prevent constipation, even though it is not digested for energy?
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre is not digested for energy, but it adds bulk that helps food move smoothly through the digestive system and prevents constipation.

questions.prompt: In the human body, which organ has the main job of cleaning the blood by removing dissolved wastes to form urine?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter the blood and remove dissolved waste substances as urine; the heart only pumps blood and does not clean it.

questions.prompt: Tiny air sacs in the lungs are surrounded by very many small blood vessels and have extremely thin walls. The main advantage of this structure is that it:
options: Stops air from entering the lungs
Speeds up the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between air and blood
questions.explanation: Thin walls and a rich blood supply give a large surface and a short distance for gases to cross, so oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged quickly between air and blood.

questions.prompt: Vaccination protects a person from a disease by:
options: Giving the body energy to fight any illness
Killing every type of germ in the body permanently
Training the body's defences to recognise and fight a particular germ quickly if it appears
Replacing the blood with clean water
questions.explanation: A vaccine exposes the body's defence system to a harmless form or part of a germ, so the body learns to recognise it and can respond fast if the real germ ever invades.

questions.prompt: In a village, many children fall ill after drinking from a shared water source. Which single action would most directly reduce the spread of this water-borne disease?
options: Encouraging the children to sleep longer
Boiling or otherwise treating the water before drinking it
Giving everyone extra sugar in their food
Asking the children to exercise more
questions.explanation: Water-borne diseases spread through contaminated water, so treating the water by boiling or other means kills the germs and most directly breaks the chain of infection.
